introduction-the-physical-office.core: An office network is cabling, switches, Wi-Fi access points, a firewall/router and core services (DHCP, DNS). On top sit segmentation (VLANs), loop prevention (STP), access control (802.1X), protections against rogue devices (DHCP snooping) and remote connectivity (VPNs). Getting the physical and L2 layers right prevents most 'the internet is slow' tickets.

first_principles.problem: A growing office's flat network lets guests, printers and finance laptops all talk to each other, and a looped cable takes it down.
truths: Physical and L2 issues dominate office outages.

analogy.title: Plumbing and rooms in a building
analogy.story: Pipes (cables) and valves (switches) must be sound, and rooms (VLANs) keep different activities separate.
analogy.breaks: Plumbing leaks are visible; broadcast storms are not until everything stops.

example.title: Typical layout
flow: Access switches per floor (PoE for APs/phones)
VLANs: staff, guest, voice, IoT, servers

check.q: Why are flat office networks risky?
check.a: Any compromised device can reach every other device, and broadcast problems affect everyone.

vlans-in-the-office-segmentation.core: VLANs split one physical switch fabric into separate broadcast domains. Access ports belong to one VLAN (for example staff 10, guest 20, voice 30); trunk ports carry several VLANs tagged with 802.1Q between switches and to the router or firewall. Traffic between VLANs must be routed, which is where firewall policy applies: guests reach only the internet, IoT can't reach finance.

first_principles.problem: Smart TVs and printers on the staff network become an entry point for malware to reach laptops.
truths: Tags identify VLANs on shared links.

analogy.title: Coloured lanes in a shared building
analogy.story: Everyone uses the same corridors, but coloured lanes keep departments separate, and crossing requires passing reception.
analogy.breaks: Lanes are visual; misconfigured trunks silently join VLANs.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Ports isolated; uplink carries only needed VLANs.

code.text:
vlan 10
 name STAFF
vlan 20
 name GUEST
interface Gi1/0/5
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
interface Gi1/0/48
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30
 switchport trunk native vlan 999

check.q: Why set the trunk native VLAN to an unused ID?
check.a: To mitigate VLAN-hopping attacks that exploit untagged native VLAN traffic.

spanning-tree-protocol-preventing-broadc.core: Redundant links between switches create loops, and Ethernet frames have no TTL. A broadcast circulates forever, multiplying until links and CPUs saturate (a broadcast storm). STP elects a root bridge and blocks redundant ports, leaving a loop-free tree, and unblocks them if an active link fails. RSTP converges in seconds. Edge ports use PortFast plus BPDU Guard so a user's looped cable gets shut down instead of melting the network.

first_principles.problem: Someone plugs both ends of a cable into the same desk switch and the whole office network collapses.

analogy.title: One-way signs on a ring road
analogy.story: Blocking one segment prevents cars circling forever; if a road closes, the sign is removed to restore a route.
analogy.breaks: Cars stop when lost; frames circulate until switches fail.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: A looped desk cable err-disables one port, not the office.

code.text:
spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst
spanning-tree vlan 1-4094 priority 4096     ! on core: become root
interface range Gi1/0/1-46
 spanning-tree portfast
 spanning-tree bpduguard enable
 storm-control broadcast level 5.00

check.q: What does BPDU Guard do on an edge port?
check.a: Shuts the port down if it receives a spanning-tree BPDU, indicating a switch or loop where only end devices should be.

dhcp-snooping-the-rogue-router.core: Any device can run a DHCP server, and a rogue one (a home router plugged in backwards, or an attacker) can hand out its own gateway and DNS, hijacking traffic. DHCP snooping marks only uplink ports toward real DHCP servers as trusted and drops DHCP offers arriving on untrusted ports. It also builds a binding table (MAC, IP, port) that Dynamic ARP Inspection and IP Source Guard use to block spoofing.

first_principles.problem: Users suddenly get 192.168.0.x addresses and no internet because someone plugged a consumer router into a wall port.
truths: Switches know which ports lead to servers.

analogy.title: Only accepting keys from the official front desk
analogy.story: If someone in the corridor hands you a room key, the building ignores it.
analogy.breaks: Guests can check badges; DHCP clients can't, so the switch must.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Rogue offers dropped; ARP spoofing blocked.

code.text:
ip dhcp snooping
ip dhcp snooping vlan 10,20,30
interface Gi1/0/48
 ip dhcp snooping trust          ! uplink to DHCP server
interface range Gi1/0/1-46
 ip dhcp snooping limit rate 15
ip arp inspection vlan 10,20,30

check.q: Which switch feature uses the DHCP snooping binding table to stop ARP spoofing?

8021x-port-based-network-access-control.core: 802.1X makes a switch port or Wi-Fi SSID authenticate a device before granting access. The supplicant (device) talks EAP to the authenticator (switch or AP), which relays to a RADIUS server checking certificates (EAP-TLS) or credentials. On success, RADIUS can assign a VLAN or ACL dynamically. Devices that can't do 802.1X (printers) use MAB with tight policies.

first_principles.problem: Anyone can plug a laptop into a meeting-room port and land on the internal network.
truths: Devices can prove identity with certificates.
Policy can be assigned per identity.
derivation: Enable **802.1X on access ports and Wi-Fi**.

analogy.title: A badge reader on every door
analogy.story: The door won't open until your badge is checked, and the badge decides which floors you can reach.
analogy.breaks: Badges can be lent; certificates should be device-bound (TPM).

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Unknown devices get no access; known ones land in the right VLAN.

code.text:
aaa new-model
aaa authentication dot1x default group radius
dot1x system-auth-control
radius server ISE
 address ipv4 10.0.50.10 auth-port 1812
 key <secret>
interface Gi1/0/12
 switchport mode access
 authentication port-control auto
 dot1x pae authenticator
 mab

check.q: Why is EAP-TLS preferred over PEAP-MSCHAPv2?
check.a: It uses mutual certificate authentication, avoiding password capture and offline cracking risks of MSCHAPv2.

wifi-basics-the-alphabet-soup-80211.core: Wi-Fi standards are Wi-Fi 4 (802.11n), 5 (ac), 6 and 6E (ax, adding the 6 GHz band) and 7 (be). Real throughput depends on band (2.4 GHz has long range, few channels and congestion; 5 and 6 GHz are faster with shorter range), channel width, co-channel interference and client count, since airtime is shared. Good office design means many lower-power APs, non-overlapping channels, WPA3, and SSIDs mapped to VLANs.

first_principles.problem: A single powerful AP covers the office but users get terrible speeds in meetings with 40 laptops.

analogy.title: A meeting room where only one person talks at a time
analogy.story: More people means less time each; more rooms (APs/channels) lets more conversations happen.
analogy.breaks: People take polite turns; Wi-Fi uses contention and retries.

code.text:
nmcli -f SSID,CHAN,FREQ,SIGNAL,SECURITY dev wifi list
# Office  36  5180 MHz  78  WPA3
# Office  1   2412 MHz  92  WPA3
# Neighbor 36 5180 MHz  60  WPA2   ← co-channel interference

check.q: Why does adding more SSIDs reduce Wi-Fi performance?
check.a: Each SSID sends beacons that consume airtime on every channel, leaving less for data.

vpns-client-vs-site-to-site.core: Site-to-site VPNs permanently connect whole networks (office to data centre or cloud) between gateways, invisible to users. Client (remote-access) VPNs connect individual devices to the office network, authenticating users, often with MFA. Full-tunnel sends all traffic through the office; split-tunnel sends only corporate subnets. Zero-trust access (ZTNA) increasingly replaces broad client VPN access with per-application access.

first_principles.problem: Remote workers on a full-tunnel VPN saturate the office internet link while streaming video calls.
truths: Networks and individuals have different needs.

analogy.title: A private road between buildings vs personal keycards
analogy.story: The road permanently links sites; keycards let individuals in from anywhere.
analogy.breaks: Keycards don't route your other traffic; full-tunnel VPNs do.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Corporate traffic tunnelled; video calls go direct.

code.text:
[Interface]
PrivateKey = <client-key>
Address = 10.99.0.15/32
DNS = 10.0.0.2
[Peer]
PublicKey = <gateway-key>
Endpoint = vpn.acme.com:51820
AllowedIPs = 10.0.0.0/16, 10.20.0.0/16   # only corporate subnets

check.q: What's the trade-off of split tunnelling?
check.a: It saves bandwidth and latency but internet traffic bypasses corporate security controls.
